units.text: 11. The survey results are advisory in nature.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 46

units.text: 12. The survey results must be made public.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 46

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.label: Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 1. Public hearings may be held throughout the municipality to discuss draft municipal legal acts on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, with the participation of municipal residents.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 2. The following must be submitted to public hearings:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 1) the draft municipal charter and a draft municipal regulatory legal act amending or supplementing that charter, except where amendments to the charter exactly reproduce provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or the constitution (charter) or laws of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation in order to bring the charter into conformity with those regulatory legal acts;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 2) the draft local budget and the report on its execution;
units.label: Point 2 Part 2 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 3) matters concerning transformation of the municipality.
units.label: Point 3 Part 2 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 3. Municipal residents aged eighteen or over have the right to participate in public hearings.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 4. Public hearings are held at the initiative of:
units.label: Part 4 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 1) the municipal representative body;
units.label: Point 1 Part 4 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 2) the head of the municipality;
units.label: Point 2 Part 4 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 3) the head of the local administration;
units.label: Point 3 Part 4 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 4) municipal residents.
units.label: Point 4 Part 4 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 5. The procedure for calling and conducting public hearings is determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 6. The procedure for public hearings must provide for notification of municipal residents of the time and place of the hearings and access to the draft municipal legal act, including by posting it on the official website of the local self-government body on the Internet information and telecommunications network, at least 10 days before the hearings; opportunities for residents to submit comments and proposals on the draft submitted for discussion, including through that official website; and other measures ensuring municipal residents’ participation in public hearings.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 7. Regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body may provide that, to post the materials and information specified in part 6 of this Article, enable municipal residents to submit comments and proposals on a draft municipal legal act, and allow them to participate in public hearings, while complying with the requirement to use the local self-government body’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network for those purposes, the federal state information system “Unified Portal of State and Municipal Services (Functions)” may be used. The procedure for using that system for the purposes of this Article is established by the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 8. Public hearings held at the initiative of municipal residents or the municipal representative body are called by the representative body; public hearings held at the initiative of the head of the municipality or the head of the local administration are called by the head of the municipality.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 9. The municipal representative body or the head of the municipality must decide to call public hearings within 10 days after receiving an initiative provided for in part 4 of this Article.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 10. Public hearings or public discussions are held in accordance with urban development legislation on draft master plans; draft land use and development rules; draft territorial layout plans; draft territorial land parcel boundary plans; draft territorial improvement and upkeep rules; drafts amending any of those approved documents; draft decisions granting permission for a conditionally permitted use of a land plot or capital construction facility; draft decisions permitting deviations from the limiting parameters of permitted construction or reconstruction of capital construction facilities; and changes from one permitted use of land plots or capital construction facilities to another in the absence of approved land use and development rules.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 11. The municipal representative body must consider the results of public hearings and public discussions when considering draft municipal legal acts.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 12. The results of public hearings and public discussions, including reasoned explanations of the decisions taken, must be made public.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 47

units.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 13. The results of public hearings and public discussions are advisory in nature.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 47

units.text: Article 48. Citizens’ meeting
units.label: Art. 48

units.text: 1. Citizens’ meetings may be held:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 1) to discuss matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life;
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 2) to inform the population about the activities of local self-government bodies and officials;
units.label: Point 2 Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 3) throughout the municipality or in part of its territory, to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for an initiative project;
units.label: Point 3 Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 4) in a rural settlement, to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to consider early termination of the elder’s powers;
units.label: Point 4 Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 5) to exercise territorial public self-government in part of the municipality’s territory.
units.label: Point 5 Part 1 Art. 48

units.text: 2. A citizens’ meeting is held at the initiative of the population, the municipal representative body or the head of the municipality, and also in the cases provided for by the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 48

units.text: 3. A citizens’ meeting held at the initiative of the municipal representative body or the head of the municipality is called by the representative body or the head of the municipality.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 48

units.text: 4. A citizens’ meeting held at the initiative of the population is called by the municipal representative body in accordance with the procedure established by its regulatory legal act.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 48

units.text: 5. The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting, and its powers, are determined by this Federal Law, regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 48

units.text: 6. The procedure for calling and holding citizens’ meetings provided for in points 1–4 of part 1 of this Article is determined by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 48

units.text: 7. The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting for the exercise of territorial public self-government is determined by the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 48

units.text: 8. Residents aged eighteen or over of the relevant territory may participate in a citizens’ meeting held throughout the municipality or in part of its territory to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for an initiative project.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 48

units.text: 9. A citizens’ meeting held in a rural settlement to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to consider early termination of the elder’s powers may be attended by citizens of the Russian Federation who reside in that settlement and have the right to vote, and also, where municipal regulatory legal acts so provide in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, by citizens of the Russian Federation aged eighteen or over on the date of the meeting who own residential premises in that rural settlement.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 48

units.text: 10. A decision to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to terminate the elder’s powers early is adopted by a majority of votes of the participants in the citizens’ meeting.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 48

units.text: 11. A citizens’ meeting may adopt appeals to local self-government bodies and officials and elect persons authorized to represent the meeting in relations with those bodies and officials.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 48

units.text: 12. A citizens’ meeting held on matters relating to territorial public self-government adopts decisions on matters assigned to its competence by the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 48

units.text: 13. Appeals adopted by a citizens’ meeting must be considered by the local self-government bodies and officials competent to resolve the matters raised, and a written reply must be sent.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 48

units.text: 14. The outcomes of a citizens’ meeting must be officially made public.
units.label: Part 14 Art. 48

units.text: Article 49. Initiative projects
units.label: Art. 49

units.text: 1. An initiative project may be submitted to the local administration, including through a territorial body of the local administration, to implement measures of priority importance to residents of the municipality or part of it, addressing matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life or other matters that local self-government bodies are entitled to resolve.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 49

units.text: 2. The procedure for determining the part of a municipality’s territory in which initiative projects may be implemented is established by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 49

units.text: 3. An initiative project may be proposed by an initiative group of at least 10 citizens aged eighteen or over who reside in the municipality concerned, territorial public self-government bodies, or a rural settlement elder (hereinafter, project initiators). The minimum size of an initiative group may be reduced by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body. A regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body may also grant the right to act as a project initiator to other persons conducting activities in the municipality concerned.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 49

units.text: 4. An initiative project must contain the following information:
units.label: Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 1) a description of the problem whose resolution is of priority importance to residents of the municipality or part of it;
units.label: Point 1 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 2) justification of the proposals for resolving that problem;
units.label: Point 2 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 3) a description of the expected outcome or outcomes of the initiative project;
units.label: Point 3 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 4) a preliminary estimate of the expenditure necessary to implement the initiative project;
units.label: Point 4 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 5) the planned implementation timetable for the initiative project;
units.label: Point 5 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 6) information on planned (possible) financial, property and/or labor contributions by interested persons to implementation of the project;
units.label: Point 6 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 7) the amount of local budget funds, if such funds are expected to be used to implement the initiative project, excluding the planned amount of initiative contributions;
units.label: Point 7 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 8) identification of the territory of the municipality or part of it within which the initiative project will be implemented, in accordance with the procedure established by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body;
units.label: Point 8 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 9) other information provided for by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.
units.label: Point 9 Part 4 Art. 49

units.text: 5. Before submission to the local administration, an initiative project must be considered at a citizens’ assembly or meeting, including a citizens’ meeting on the exercise of territorial public self-government in part of the municipality, to discuss the project, determine whether it meets the interests of residents of the municipality or part of it and whether its implementation is appropriate, and adopt a decision of the assembly or meeting supporting it. Several initiative projects may be considered at the same citizens’ assembly or meeting.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 49

units.text: 6. In addition to the mandatory support for an initiative project provided for in part 5 of this Article, a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body may provide for further ascertainment of citizens’ opinions on support for the project through a citizens’ survey and/or other means of ascertaining public opinion.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 49

units.text: 7. When submitting an initiative project to the local administration, project initiators attach the minutes of the citizens’ assembly or meeting and the results of further ascertainment of citizens’ opinions through a survey and/or other means, confirming support for the project by residents of the municipality or part of it.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 49

units.text: 8. Information on submission of an initiative project to the local administration must be made public, including by posting on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network, within three working days after submission. It must contain the information specified in part 4 of this Article and information about the project initiators. At the same time, citizens are informed of the opportunity to submit comments and proposals on the project to the local administration, with a submission period of at least five working days. Municipal residents aged eighteen or over may submit comments and proposals. In a rural settlement, the rural settlement elder may bring this information to citizens’ attention.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 49

units.text: 9. The local administration must consider an initiative project within 30 days after its submission. Following consideration, the local administration adopts one of the following decisions:
units.label: Part 9 Art. 49

units.text: 1) support the initiative project and continue work on it within the budget appropriations provided for the relevant purposes by the local budget decision and/or in accordance with the procedure for preparing and considering the draft local budget (amending the local budget decision);
units.label: Point 1 Part 9 Art. 49

units.text: 2) refuse to support the initiative project and return it to the project initiators, stating the reasons for refusal.
units.label: Point 2 Part 9 Art. 49
